I received 3 quotations in response to my solicitations, 2 of which were competitive in terms of price, product quality etc. I then followed up with an site meeting, a discussion regarding the timing of the work, specifications, rooftop layout, positioning of inverter & so forthTo be honest we could have proceeded with either firms. The decision to run with Apex was down to the 60/40 split of the 22 panels to maximise the solar harvesting Sun up/down, the relocation of the new smart inverter from a gyprock wall in the garage to a brick wall (for added safety) and the polite/courteous manner of the sales person initially and, subsequently, the Apex team who were on site for 2 days. Day 1 was primarily spent removing the then existing system and preparing the additional cabling due to the resiting of the inverter. Unlike the other businesses the Apex electrician insisted on the new cabling being hidden within the ceiling voids rather than being visible. A nice gesture!Initially I reacted adversely to the battery sited on the garage floor rather than the more common siting hung on the wall near the inverter (visions of the Tesla power wall). Once the electrician pointed out the benefits of being able to add more storage on the stacked module I realised the obvious benefit. As an aside it is silent and operates without emitting heat. Neighbours' power walls emit a hum or buzz  & are fitted to external masonry walls. With houses now being erected almost gutter to gutter this is an important consideration for some folk.In summary, the answer to all of your questions is YES, noting that this system has been operational for just 14 days. Allow for around 42 days from the time you pay the 10% deposit to installation. Our battery was activated at 4:10 PM on the Monday and at 8:30 AM the next day the battery was fully charged. We were impressed by Apex.
Installation team tidy and respectful. Process for a new meter to be installed progressed on our behalf.

Tim from Apex Solar called me the next morning after I requested the three quotes, super fast.Install done clean, ran cables through my existing conduit and installed new lower wattage element in my hot water system with timer, this is just done as part of the service, I didn’t even know about this extra power saving feature.Apex arranged the grid connection with the power company on our behalf which will happen next Tuesday.

I spent a bit of time researching the ideal system for my needs and Tim from Apex was happy to accomodate. He's very knowledgable and experienced and provided me some great recommendations. I selected them under the assumption Tim would be there on the day of install. The day arrived and he was unable to attend. The roofers and electricians were apparently unaware of everything Tim an I had discussed. I was questioned why I'd want a network cable ran from the inverter and told they only had a bulky meter box to install. I briefly ran the roofers through the panel placement and selected a great spot for the inverter and battery install with the help of the electricians.The panel install by the roofers was completed in half a day, the roofers left without saying goodbye or offering an inspection of the work. I was disappointed to see the panel placement wasn't optimised for for the path of the sun. Some sort of sealant was also spilled on the roof without my knowledge. Zip ties were still being found in my yard months after the install.The electricians spent the entire day doing the inverter, battery and wiring installation. It was getting close to 5pm and the electricians informed me that there was a black out (what are the odds) and would be unable to finish commissioning the inverter. They told me that someone else, maybe not them, would be back sometime to finish it off. I asked if power would be restored to the house when the black out ends, I was assured yes it would. Hours went by and I noticed neighbours lights turning on as it got dark. I checked the meter box at the front of the property and grid power was restored, but not to the house Turns out they forgot to switch the main meter back on after leaving...The next day was spent on the phone to Tim as he apologised and walked me through the commissioning which, thankfully, I was able to do myself. The system was up and running... sort of. I soon discovered the inverter throwing "over voltage" errors which would cause the system to shut down for up to an hour at a time. Turns out the voltage coming back from the grid was over the "safe" limits and would have to be fixed by the wholesaler. Tim's team lodged a fault and it was fixed up a couple of months later. I believe this should have been checked before the install.The next issue came upon inspecting the wiring that was done under the house. Bare wires were bundled together that drooped and cut corners. Insulation was ripped out and left on the ground. It looked very unprofessional. Tim did return with the electrician who did it initially and instructed him to fix it up while he tested the previously mentioned over voltage issue. Unfortunately it still wasn't good enough. I contacted Apex again and requested it be done with conduit. I paid extra for the required materials.Months went by, the grid voltage issue now fixed I continued to experience more voltage issues, where the system would shut down for up to an hour at a time. I did a lot of back and forth with Apex and then directly with Fronius. In the end I was able to determine the voltage was too high on one of the strings and Fronius informed me that the 12x REC 440W panels had been configured incorrectly, voiding the warranty of the inverter. I let Apex know and they promptly came out and fixed it. Since then the system has been solid. Unfortunately this took 1 year to fully resolve.As it stands, I have a solid system I am happy with. The panel placement on the West-facing roof is still not ideal, however. The meter box is installed in a room and makes a constant HUMMMM which is apparently normal (??).I'd recommend Apex but only if you get everything in writing beforehand: Panel placement, meter box type and size, double check the configuration, agree on wiring and inverter placement. Check grid voltage well before the install date. Insist Tim is there on the install date. Avoid a year of headaches like me.

We are located on NSW mid-north coast - there are installers around, but very few are registered with Solar Quotes.  In fact, there was only one local installer based between Taree and Port Macquarie:  Apex Solar.  The whole process of design through to installation has been a breeze:  Tim and Gemma and their team have been so easy to deal with, so helpful, and the performance of their solution for our south-facing hill which is shaded by trees has exceeded expectations.  From the start, Tim was able to design a system which met our requirements - we are grid-connected but subject to intermittent black-outs, and wanted to avoid products that have been flagged as manufactured with slave labour (sadly, products from some countries are affected).  Tim rose to the challenges and six weeks after midwinter, we have a system which is meeting household requirements with minimal purchase from the grid.  Eight weeks after midwinter, we are re-charging batteries fully and exporting to the grid - not that export makes any money, but there are feel-good benefits!  Overall, we experienced none of the pitfalls of shoddy manufacture, design or installation which were raised recently by ABC news coverage.  So the message is, don't hesitate to install panels and batteries if you can rely upon a quality installer like Apex.  Hope that the underlying enthusiasm doesn't make me sound like I've been taken hostage by a cult!

We had a complex install due to our roof shape, shading issues, requirement to support a generator now and batteries in future. I was fairly particular about what I wanted to achieve and in general have pretty high standards. I found Tim to be very relaxed, friendly and helpful during the quoting process and he seemed happy to spend the time discussing the system design with me. I had 3 quotes (2 through solar quotes and 1 directly with a highly regarded local installer) - all options seemed to be reputable installers using good quality gear, but I felt most comfortable dealing with Tim and felt his system design was the best for my situation. After months of to and fro and waiting on the installer I'd approached before coming to Solar Quotes they ended up arriving at a nearly identical design (& brands) to Tim's, but Tim was cheaper and arrived at that point immediately and without a fuss over the supposed difficulty of what I was asking for. He used top quality brands and I was happy with the installation he and the boys did, their electrical workmanship was very neat (rare for me to say that) and Tim kept in constant communication during the install to make sure I was happy and was willing to make changes to a couple of the panel positions along the way. If I had to fault him on anything, I wasn't sure exactly when he was going to come and do the install, but I know he's at the mercy of the weather so i guess that's to be expected. I'd be confident recommending Apex Solar to anyone looking for an installer - Tim has a can-do approach and seems to me like the sort of guy who will make sure the end outcome is something you're happy with.
